summary: The finite-epsilon distributional scaling used in the central volume-identity proof has boundary coefficient a^2c instead of ac. An admissible unit disk gives a singular-measure discrepancy11/40. Correcting this coefficient changes the limiting boundary integral by O(epsilon) and does not refute the rigidity conclusions. Documented sign corrections are separately reproduced.

problems.title: Surface-measure coefficient in the finite-difference Laplacian

claim.location: Primary PDF p7, unnumbered Delta phi_epsilon formula before(2.6); exponent3-n in(2.6)-(2.7),pp7-8; slit analoguep14
claim.text: For u(ax), the singular coefficient on a^-1 reduced boundary is printed a^2 c.

assumptions: Bounded finite-perimeter domain with upper surface-density bound(1.4).
u in W1,2(Rn),zero outside,Delta u=c H^(n-1)|boundary-1_Omega dx.
Counterexample uses n2,unitdisk,c1/2,u=(1-r²)_+/4,epsilon1/10; all stated assumptions met.
problems.check: Distributional change of variables gives Delta[u(a.)]=ac H^(n-1)|a^-1 boundary-a²1_a^-1Omega dx. At r10/11 the only derivative jump in phi_epsilon has coefficient11/4, whereas printed121/40.
problems.result: False finite-epsilon distributional identity; discrepancy11/40 cannot be absorbed by an absolutely continuous remainder.
counterevidence: Actual source images confirm squared coefficients.
The correction changes inverse-dilation quotient exponent3-n to2-n, whose boundary difference equals half[a^(2-n)u(x/a)+b^(2-n)u(x/b)]=O(epsilon).
Finite surface measure makes the integrated difference vanish; no counterexample to Theorem1.3 or4.1 is established.
Known author erratum addresses separate signs and labels, not this scaling coefficient; no first-discovery claim.

correction.text: Use ac for the rescaled surface coefficient and2-n for the inverse-dilation exponent; retain corrected author sign. Finite-epsilon identity and its unchanged boundary limit checked.

checks.independent_derivation: For a=1+epsilon and Delta u=-1_Omega+c H^(n-1)|boundary, scaling Delta[u(a x)] multiplies the volume density by a^2 and the hypersurface measure by a, not a^2. The n=2 unit-disk solution u=(1-|x|^2)_+/4 has c=1/2 and satisfies the stated bounded indecomposable finite-perimeter and Lipschitz assumptions. At epsilon=1/10 the reported singular coefficient is 121/40 instead of 11/4, a nonzero difference of 11/40 that no absolutely continuous remainder absorbs.
checks.result: The displayed exact identity is false under its real hypotheses.

checks.claim: Effect on the limiting argument and severity
checks.independent_derivation: The corrected boundary quotient uses powers 2-n instead of 3-n. Their difference equals one half of the sum of the two scaled boundary traces with powers 2-n. Since u vanishes on the boundary and is Lipschitz on bounded Omega, this is O(epsilon) in L1 of the finite boundary measure. The limiting identity therefore admits the report's repair.
checks.result: Major is justified by an invalid central derivation, without claiming that the final Serrin theorem is false.

checks.claim: Erratum, normal orientation and revised manuscript counterevidence
checks.independent_derivation: With inward normal, integral nu dot x = -n|Omega|. The corrected limits phi=ct/2, quotient=-ct/2 and psi=ct give the positive integrated identity. The retained erratum corrects this sign, the slit boundary notation and Lemma 4.4 label. The 2026-03-09 author manuscript fixes those items but retains the separate finite-scale squared surface coefficient/power issue on the checked pages.
checks.result: Known corrections are not presented as new discoveries; adoption of the scaling repair in a journal VoR remains unverified.

checks.independent_derivation: The equal two-sided blow-up c|nu dot z| in (4.3) is explicitly needed for slit cancellation. With Delta u=-1, Delta P=2|D^2u|^2-2/n=2|D^2u+I/n|^2; an intermediate printed sign does not invalidate the final square identity.
